title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own writing. It is page 74 of an English typescript, with formulas filled in by hand, that has been filed in cote 15. The style ('cross-section', 'the group H^0', 'basis (not necessarily of linearly independent vectors)', sheaves written O_V[nE], local trivialisations on a cover U^{(i)}) reads like an English translation of a Russian or Kodaira-school paper on complex or algebraic varieties. The likely topic is contracting subvarieties or projective embedding. The next archive page (the 'Définition: Soit K/Q galoisienne … σ²=1' fragment, faint show-through from a recto) is unrelated to it.

The mathematics, in modern terms:
- V is a compact variety, E a divisor, and ℰ_φ a subvariety (probably the fibre or exceptional locus of a map φ). O_V[nE] is the line bundle O(nE), and Φ^{(i)} is the local function representing a section Φ on the chart U^{(i)}.
- End of a lemma (presumably Lemma 3). From a cohomology vanishing (displayed as H^1(ℰ_φ, O(nE)|_ℰ)=0), the restriction sequence gives a surjection r*: H^0(V,O(nE)) → H^0(ℰ_φ, O(nE)|_ℰ) (19).
- Suppose some P∈ℰ_φ were a base point of |nE|, i.e. every global section vanishes at P. Every section on ℰ_φ is a restriction r*Φ, and restriction on stalks is restriction of functions, so every section of O(nE)|_ℰ would vanish at P.
- This contradicts the fact that O(nE)|_ℰ is globally generated for n ≥ n(ℰ_φ). Conclusion: for n large, |nE| has no base points along ℰ_φ.
- Return to Theorem 2. Set E' = n_ℰ E. Take a spanning set Φ_0,…,Φ_T of H^0(V, O(nE')) and define f_n: V → P^T by P ↦ (Φ_0^{(i)}(P):…:Φ_T^{(i)}(P)) for P∈U^{(i)}. This is the standard morphism given by a base-point-free linear system.

Purpose: constructing a morphism to projective space from a semi-ample or nef-type divisor, in a contraction or projectivity criterion.
errors: As written, surjectivity of r* does not follow from H^1(ℰ_φ, O(nE)|_ℰ)=0. From 0→I_ℰ(nE)→O_V(nE)→O_ℰ(nE)→0 one needs H^1(V, I_ℰ⊗O(nE))=0. Either the hypothesis was stated differently on the previous (missing) page of the typescript, or the hand-filled formula is a slip or abbreviation.
'Basis (not necessarily of linearly independent vectors)' means a spanning set. Terminological only.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of a typed English translation of someone else's paper on complex or algebraic geometry, misfiled among Grothendieck's motivic Galois notes. Its content is a routine base-point-freeness argument and nothing on it is Grothendieck's.
transcription_corrections: The typed subscript rendered as ℰ_ω-like is the same ℰ_φ as in the handwritten formulas; the transcription's uniform use of ℰ_φ is correct.

The 'NEXT PAGE' transcription describes a faint show-through from a different document (Galois/real structures). It is not a continuation of this typescript, which breaks off at 'if P ∈ V, P ∈ U^{(i)}, then'.
